A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 13-page OORL/GEPO study. The full text, equations, Figures 1–3, Tables 1–4, and Appendices A–C are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3-8B-OORL evaluations on MultiPL-E and CrossPLEval, alongside component ablations, in Section 4 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and component-ablation results in Section 4 and Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same binary-reward on-policy training, GEPO group preferences and winner-group variance penalty, and combined OORL objective. No algorithm, component, or training-objective changes appear.

E1.justification: Both versions use SYNTHETIC-1 and APPS for code-translation training, SLTrans for C-to-IR preferences, and MultiPL-E and CrossPLEval for evaluation. The training and evaluation languages and task coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain DS-Coder-V2-Lite-Inst, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Inst, and Qwen3-8B as comparators. Table 4 retains the same REINFORCE++ alone, REINFORCE++ with DPO, and REINFORCE++ with GEPO comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains pass@1 evaluation, Qwen3-8B non-thinking mode, identical training and benchmark sample counts, and the same one-epoch training budget. No evaluation procedures or experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Table 4 contain the same ablations testing on-policy training and the additional contribution of DPO versus GEPO. No robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or supplementary case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged, including OORL's 76.31 MultiPL-E score and 63.15 CrossPLEval average in Table 4. Figure 3 retains identical plotted values despite its changed colors and sizing.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Sections 2–3, including the GEPO variance constraint, are identical. Appendix B retains the same implicit-reward derivation and Equations 11–15.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about OORL, GEPO's modeling of functional equivalence, and improved multilingual code understanding and generation.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 retain the same generalization and functional-equivalence interpretations. Appendix C preserves the limitation concerning GEPO's GPU-memory requirements and the memory-versus-latency tradeoff of processing responses sequentially.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including AdamW at 5 × 10^-7, batch size 8, sequence length 8192, DeepSpeed ZeRO stage 2 with offload, and four 80 GB A100 GPUs. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 27 references and Appendix A related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to preference-optimization methods and IR-based code models is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 19 May 2025 to v2 dated 18 July 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, section order, and appendix structure otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Figure 3's radar plots and legend switch to lighter colors and slightly smaller sizing, accompanied by small spacing shifts around Table 1 and adjacent text on page 7. Plot axes, labels, values, and captions are retained; other figures, tables, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, and appendices are unchanged. Figure 3's cosmetic restyling and the updated version stamp do not resolve a substantive deficiency or establish a meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
